about.title: Carlsbad Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Carlsbad's mix of coastal walkways, outlet shopping, hotel properties and hillside neighborhoods means people spend much of the day on ground someone else is responsible for maintaining. A wet tile floor near a Carlsbad Boulevard cafe, an unmarked step at a Palomar Airport Road business park, loose pavers at an El Camino Real shopping center, or a dim stairwell in a rental complex can all turn an ordinary errand into weeks of recovery. Under California premises liability law, the question is rarely whether you fell; it is whether the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and did nothing to fix it or warn you. Photos of the spot, the names of anyone who saw it, and a prompt written request to preserve surveillance footage can make an enormous difference, because video is often overwritten within days. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Carlsbad residents and visitors with an independent personal injury attorney who handles premises cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Carlsbad Fall Victims Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Notice is the whole case
items.desc: California requires proof that the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney in our network knows how to pull inspection logs, maintenance records and prior complaints that show how long a problem was left alone.

items.title: Video disappears fast
items.desc: Stores, hotels and apartment complexes along El Camino Real and Palomar Airport Road routinely overwrite footage within days. Getting a preservation letter out early is one of the first things a connected attorney will do.

items.title: Deadlines and shared fault handled
items.desc: You generally have two years to file, but far less when a Carlsbad city or San Diego County property is involved. Under pure comparative fault, being partly to blame reduces a claim rather than ending it, and an attorney can push back on inflated blame.

items.question: I slipped on a wet walkway near the beach along Carlsbad Boulevard. Does it matter who owns that stretch?
items.answer: Yes, a great deal. If the area belongs to the City of Carlsbad, the State, or another public entity, a government claim usually has to be filed within six months, far sooner than the two-year deadline for private property. An attorney can help pin down ownership quickly so nothing lapses while you recover.

items.question: The store says I should have watched where I was going. Do I still have a claim?
items.answer: Possibly. California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you share some responsibility your claim is reduced by that percentage rather than thrown out. Whether the owner had notice of the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it remains the central issue.

items.question: What should I do in the first few days after a fall in Carlsbad?
items.answer: Get medical care first, then photograph the exact spot and whatever caused the fall, if you can. Ask the property for an incident report and write down the names of any witnesses. Request in writing that any surveillance video be preserved, since many systems erase footage within a week or two.
